messages:
maya: Thinking through a dual-pkg publishing strategy for our JS/TS SDK. Main constraints: ESM-first for edge (Vercel/Deno), CJS for Node consumers, and Typescript consumers keep hitting "types not found" with conditional exports. Anyone got battle-tested patterns? :thinking:

alex: We did this at my last job. Short version: use an exports map for import/require, provide a top-level "types" field, and publish both ESM and CJS builds. Also keep an ESM-only tiny build for edge. Example package.json snippet we used:

```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference",
  "version": "X.Y.Z",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
  "module": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

jenny: Heads-up — TS + bundlers can still be picky. Some toolchains (older rollup/vite/tsc combos) won't look inside the exports map for types unless you also have the top-level "types" pointer. We had to add both the top-level "types" and the "types" inside the exports entry to make consumers happy. Also ensure your .d.ts paths match exactly the exports paths.

zach: For edge runtimes specifically: keep the edge build ESM-only and avoid use of node builtins (no node:crypto, no fs). Use Web Crypto API for auth signing so the same bundle runs in Vercel Edge / Deno. Also keep auth/retry behavior lean — fetch-based client with AbortSignal and retry wrapper so edge consumers don't need node globals.

maya: We ran into onboarding friction: our Next.js Edge sample broke because the example used `require()` while the published pkg had "type": "module" and conditional exports. People copy/pasted and hit confusing errors. Two quick wins: ship two example apps (node and edge) and make the README explicit about import styles.

alex: Agreed. Proposal: default publish path = ESM (exports.import -> ./dist/esm/index.mjs), provide CJS at exports.require -> ./dist/cjs/index.cjs, ensure top-level "types" -> ./dist/index.d.ts. Also add a tiny ./dist/edge/index.mjs build (ESM only) that uses webcrypto polyfills where needed. CI should smoke-test both examples.

jenny: Build notes: build targets ->
- Rollup/tsup -> dist/esm (es2020, ESM), dist/cjs (cjs), dist/edge (es2020, no node builtins)
- Generate one consolidated index.d.ts at dist/index.d.ts
- Update npm publish script to include all three dirs and proper package.json exports map

zach: For auth + retry behavior: implement fetch-first client with optional Node-specific helpers. In node, if consumer wants native node crypto, they can opt-in via `import {nodeCrypto} from '@redwood/inference/node-helpers'` (separate path). Avoid bundling heavy node polyfills into the edge build.

maya: Action items:
- I'll open an RFC describing the exports map + types strategy + sample app changes.
- alex: can you write the docs snippet for README showing both import and require examples?
- zach: can you take edge build + rollup changes?
- jenny: can you validate TypeScript consumer tests across common bundlers (tsc, vite, next)?

alex: I can pick the README updates. I'll also add a small matrix of which runtimes to test (Node 16/18, Vercel Edge, Deno).

zach: I'll PR the rollup config and add an example Next.js Edge sample in examples/edge-next.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: created issue #412: "dual-pkg publishing RFC" and assigned to maya. :robot_face:

maya: Thanks everyone. Quick follow-up Q: should we consider publishing a single ESM-only package and provide a tiny CJS compatibility wrapper package (e.g., @redwood/inference-cjs) instead of one package with lots of exports? Pros/cons?

jenny: Tradeoffs: single-package is simpler for consumers but harder to maintain (publish pipelines + mono-build). Separate CJS shim reduces package.json export complexity but increases discoverability overhead. I'd vote single package with clear docs and CI tests.

alex: +1 single package. We can keep the exports map but provide small cjs bundle. That keeps npm install UX simple.

maya: Great. I'll capture the consensus in the RFC and list the exact package.json snippet we want to land. Thanks! :pray:
